name: Sika Intraplast-100 Z
paste:
SIKA® INTRAPLAST-100 Z: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Intraplast-100 Z, July 2026, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sika-intraplast-100z.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Intraplast-100 Z where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2026, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Intraplast-100 Z is an expanding plasticising agent used to increase fluidity and cohesion of sand/cement grouts and is suitable for use in grouting.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Pre-stressed cable ducts.
    - Rock and soil anchoring.
    - Bearing plates.
    - Preplaced aggregates.
    - Tunnel linings.
    - Tilt up construction wall panels.
    - Piling
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Intraplast-100 Z
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Expanding and plasticising admixture for cementitious grout
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (July 2026, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Intraplast-100 Z plasticises the mix allowing for a reduction in water for equal fluidity, thus improving the strength and hardened properties of the grout.
    - Gas generated during setting produces evenly distributed micro bubbles causing expansion to take place thus compensating for plastic settlement and plastic shrinkage.
    - The initial retarding effect of Sika® Intraplast-100 Z and its plasticising action greatly improves grout penetration and substantially reduces water separation and bleeding.
    - The expansive forces generated promote complete filling of voids and fissures.
    - Sika® Intraplast-100 Z produces non-hazardous gas therefore it can be used in mines and underground works.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: White powder
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 10 kg pail
    - Shelf life: Stored in the original sealed packaging at temperatures of between 5 °C and 35°C, this product will keep for at least 12 months.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C , protected from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (July 2026, Version 01.03) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2026, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Recommended dosage: Typical dosage rates are between 5 - 30 kg per cubic meter of grout depending on specific requirements. Always conduct trials before use.
4.3 Dispensing. The preferred dosage method of Sika® Intraplast-100 Z is by premixing it with the gauging water. If this is not possible it can be premixed with the dry cement/sand mixture providing it is thoroughly mixed through.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations. Suitable for Portland based cement including sulphate resistant cement.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (July 2026, Version 01.03) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Intraplast-100 Z, July 2026, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sika-intraplast-100z.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Intraplast-100 Z, version 02/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sds-sika-intraplast-100z.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Intraplast-100 Z, version 15/07/2024, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/Intraplast-100%20Z%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
